chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, who said:

I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'A man used to visit Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), and he was known as Abu Murra. So when he sought permission to enter, he would say, "Abu Murra is at the door." Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said to him: "By Allah, when you come to our door, do not say, 'Abu Murra'."'

key_terms.يُكَنَّى: to be known by a teknonym (kunya)

ai.seo_question: What is the etiquette for announcing one's name when visiting Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the nuanced etiquette (adab) of approaching the Ahl al-Bayt, where Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) instructed a frequent visitor to avoid announcing himself as 'Abu Murra' at the door. Scholars suggest this was either to prevent confusion with another prominent figure bearing the same kunya or to maintain a specific level of decorum and distinction for the Imam's private space, reflecting the high status of the Imams in Shia tradition.
